text:
alex: Quick thought — I want to propose a much smaller fallback API for the runtime/router boundary so we can ship an automatic fallback MVP without redoing the whole decision plane.

maria: Curious — what would the smaller API look like? we still need to encode why we fallback for observability/debugging.

alex: Agreed. Idea: runtime exposes two tiny primitives from the control plane: 1) fallback_rules (opaque JSON blob per route) 2) probe_token that runtime can call to validate a target variant. Then runtime keeps local cache and makes fallback decisions locally. We include a lightweight reason enum in responses: {"fallback_reason": "probe_fail|latency_budget|capacity"}.

sam: That keeps runtime ownership for immediate action (good). But where do rollout slices / weights live? control plane only? how do we guard against drift between control plane and cached runtime rules?

alex: weights remain in control plane. runtime pulls them with the blocker that rules include version ids and TTLs. If TTL expires, it falls back to safe defaults. We purposely avoid strong consistency — prefer eventual with short TTLs.

jin: TTLs sound ok but we need a failsafe for divergent semantics across model variants (e.g., different tokenization/kv behavior). maybe add a bitmask of compatibility hints in fallback_rules so runtime can detect incompatible variants and fallback preemptively.

maria: compatibility hints are sensible. Also we should add a debug header for ops: X-Redwood-Fallback: reason=probe_fail;rule_v=42;probe_latency=230ms — that will help SREs.

ops-bot: Note: adding headers may affect downstream logging/storage. Check retention/PII. Also, ops-bot automatically flagged a request to add schema docs to the console team.

sam: Tradeoff: central decision plane allows richer signals (SLO/error trends) but adds latency to decision and a new availability surface. Localizing decisions reduces RTO but duplicates logic. I think the MVP should localize safety-critical decisions and keep longer-term policy in control plane.

lia: For telemetry, runtime should emit probe outcomes and fallback events with rule_v and probe_id. That helps correlate to canary evals. Maybe we attach a short hash of the rule blob to events.

alex: Actionable plan I propose:
- short RFC (~1 page) describing API: fallback_rules schema, TTL semantics, probe_token contract, response header format (alex)
- telemetry hook: event names + fields (lia + maria)
- console/schema: UI for rule_v rollouts and read-only view (jin)
- test harness: simulate probe_fail/latency/capacity scenarios, run in staging for 2 days (sam)

maria: I'll prototype the probe_token flow — it should be a simple signed URL the runtime hits and gets 200/204 with latency info. also include rate-limit guidance in the RFC.

jin: For ownership: runtime team owns local decision code and probe client. control plane owns rule blob generation and rollout API. Console owns visualization and audit. Ops owns SLOs and alerting criteria. Call it out in RFC.

sam: One more design: introduce a "soft-fallback" mode where runtime returns candidate variant but marks it as degraded (still charges normal). That lets product teams see quality impact without taking full rollback.

alex: Nice. We'll include soft-fallback in schema: mode=hard|soft. Soft emits extra telemetry.

lia: Meeting to sync? 30m tomorrow morning to finalize RFC draft and owners.

alex: Booked — thanks everyone. I'll open the RFC in docs/rfcs and link it here when done. :thumbsup:
